title: The repair library
bodyMd:
In the fictional town of Bellmere, a library began lending household tools. Its managers expected residents to save money by borrowing equipment they used only occasionally. After a year, a survey showed that many borrowers had instead used the service to try unfamiliar repairs before deciding whether to buy tools of their own. Sales at the local hardware shop had not fallen. The shopkeeper, initially opposed to the scheme, began offering short repair demonstrations at the library.

The managers did not regard the survey as evidence that the scheme had failed. Their original explanation for its value had been too narrow: access could reduce the cost of experimenting as well as the cost of ownership. However, they resisted a proposal to judge success solely by the number of tool loans. One carefully chosen loan might enable a lasting skill, whereas repeated loans could reflect either frequent useful work or equipment that was difficult to use.
